explanation_markdown:
## Concept Overview

The mirror section of the Exemplar links ray behaviour, image size and the mirror formula. Concave mirrors can form real inverted images or, for objects inside the focal length, virtual erect enlarged images; convex mirrors give virtual erect diminished images and are useful when a wide field of view is needed. The source also tests special positions such as the centre of curvature, where a concave mirror forms an image of equal size, and the focus, where a source can produce a parallel beam. Numerical questions require correct sign convention because real object and real image distances lie in front of the mirror and are negative in the New Cartesian convention.

## Key Rules & Formulas

- **Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u using the New Cartesian sign convention.** — For a real object in front of a mirror, u is negative; a concave mirror has negative f.
- **Mirror magnification m = h_i/h_o = -v/u.** — A real inverted image has negative magnification; a virtual erect image has positive magnification.
- **For a concave mirror, an object at the centre of curvature forms a real inverted image of the same size at the centre of curvature.** — Since R=2f, this position is twice the focal length from the pole.
- **A convex mirror forms a virtual, erect and diminished image for a real object.** — This is why the source identifies it with rear-view type image behaviour.
- **A point source placed near the focus of a concave reflector can produce a nearly parallel beam.** — The source applies this to torches, search lights and vehicle headlights.

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** A 10 mm awl pin in front of a concave mirror forms a 5 mm image at 30 cm in front of the mirror. Find the focal length.

*Solution:* The image is real and inverted, so h_i/h_o=-5/10=-1/2. For mirrors, m=-v/u. With v=-30 cm, -1/2 = -(-30)/u = 30/u, so u=-60 cm. Then 1/f=1/v+1/u=-1/30-1/60=-1/20, giving f=-20 cm.

**Example 2:** Rays from the Sun converge 15 cm in front of a concave mirror. Where should an object be placed so that its image is the same size as the object?

*Solution:* Sunlight is effectively parallel, so it converges at the focus; therefore focal length magnitude is 15 cm. A concave mirror gives an image equal in size to the object when the object is at the centre of curvature, 2f from the pole. Thus the object should be placed 30 cm in front of the mirror.

**Example 3:** A child sees her head enlarged, middle portion same size and legs diminished in a “magic mirror”. What mirror combination from top to bottom produces this?

*Solution:* An enlarged erect image can be produced by a concave mirror when the object is within its focal length, so the top should be concave. A plane mirror gives same-size image, so the middle should be plane. A convex mirror gives an erect diminished image, so the lower part should be convex.

## What Makes Exemplar Questions on This Topic Harder

The Exemplar blends qualitative image recognition with quantitative sign-convention problems. Students may have to infer the mirror type from image size, use sunlight to identify focal length, or combine magnification and mirror formula. This makes image properties a reasoning tool rather than a table to memorise.

## Common Mistakes

- **Using a positive focal length for a concave mirror.** — Only the distance magnitude is remembered. *How to avoid:* Under the New Cartesian convention, concave focus lies in front of the mirror, so f is negative.
- **Using m=v/u instead of m=-v/u for mirrors.** — Lens and mirror magnification formulas are mixed. *How to avoid:* Remember the minus sign for mirror magnification.
- **Saying equal-size image occurs at the focus.** — Focus is treated as the central special point for all cases. *How to avoid:* Equal size for a concave mirror occurs at the centre of curvature, 2f.
- **Assuming a convex mirror can form a magnified real image.** — Mirror types are not linked to their consistent image character. *How to avoid:* For ordinary real objects, a convex mirror gives virtual, erect, diminished images.

## Problem-Solving Strategy

Identify the mirror type and expected image character before calculating. Assign u, v and f signs using the chosen convention. If image size is given, use m=-v/u to relate u and v, then apply the mirror formula. For special-position questions, use the physical facts: focus gives parallel/reflected behaviour, centre of curvature gives equal-size real image.

## Quick Recall

Concave: f<0, can magnify or form real images. Convex: virtual, erect, diminished. Mirror magnification has a minus sign. Equal-size concave image occurs at 2f, not at f.

## Practice Problem

**Problem:** In torches, search lights and vehicle headlights, where is the bulb placed relative to the concave reflector?

**Hint:** A source near the focus sends reflected rays out nearly parallel.

**Answer:** Very near the focus of the reflector.
